polls.description: A major controversy has erupted over Pentagon partnerships with AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic for military applications, including their use in Iran strikes and subsequent policy reversals.
polls.question: Should AI companies be required to accept Pentagon contracts?

cluster_stories.title: Anthropic Nears $20 Billion Revenue Run Rate Amid Pentagon Feud
cluster_stories.summary: Anthropic PBC is on track to generate annual revenue of almost $20 billion, a projection based on current performance, more than doubling its run rate from late last year — a sign of the AI company’s rapid growth in the lead-up to its recent clash with the Pentagon.
cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC NEARS $20B REVENUE... PENTAGON FEUD ERUPTS

cluster_stories.title: ChatGPT uninstalls surge 295% in US after OpenAI’s AI deal with Pentagon
cluster_stories.summary: ChatGPT mobile app uninstalls in the US jumped 295% day-over-day after OpenAI’s Pentagon deal. Downloads fell 13% on Saturday and 5% on Sunday, while 1-star reviews surged. Rival Anthropic’s Claude saw download growth, topped US App Store rankings, and gained strongly across several countries.
cluster_stories.headline: CHATGPT UNINSTALLS SURGE 295% After Pentagon Deal Backlash

cluster_stories.title: US uses Anthropic AI, B-2 bombers and suicide drones in Iran strikes
cluster_stories.summary: USA launched a significant military operation against Iran. The US deployed Tomahawk missiles, stealth fighters, and new one-way attack drones. For the first time, artificial intelligence tools were reportedly used in combat. B-2 stealth bombers struck underground missile facilities. The operation involved a range of advanced military technology.

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI amends Pentagon deal as Sam Altman admits it looks ‘sloppy’
cluster_stories.summary: ChatGPT owner’s CEO says it will bar its technology being used for mass surveillance or by intelligence servicesBusiness live – latest updatesOpenAI is amending its hastily arranged deal to supply artificial intelligence to the US Department of War (DoW) after the ChatGPT owner’s chief executive admitted it looked “opportunistic and sloppy”.The contract prompted fears the San Francisco startup’s AI could be used for domestic mass surveillance but its boss, Sam Altman, said on Monday night the startup would explicitly bar its technology from being used for that purpose or being deployed by defence department intelligence agencies such as the National Security Agency (NSA). Continue reading...
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI AMENDS PENTAGON DEAL... Altman Admits 'Sloppy' Move
